gaps.sentence: This bill ___ be right — we only ordered two coffees.
gaps.hint: an obvious mistake, so it is impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' shows the speaker believes something is not possible: can't be right.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ to hand in essays by Friday at the latest.
gaps.hint: ought to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' takes the full infinitive, so only 'ought' fits before 'to': ought.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ wear badges at all times inside the plant.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' = a rule that has to be followed.

gaps.sentence: You ___ to be more careful with your passwords.
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' behaves like 'should' and always takes 'to': ought to be.

gaps.sentence: I do not know whose coat this is — it ___ belong to one of the guests.
gaps.explanation: 'Might' hedges a guess when the speaker is not sure: might belong.

gaps.sentence: That ___ be Sarah at the door — she is in Berlin until Friday.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' expresses logical impossibility: can't be Sarah.

gaps.sentence: I ___ have said that — I apologised immediately.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' expresses regret about a past action: shouldn't have.

gaps.sentence: ___ we need to book, or can we just turn up?
gaps.explanation: 'Need to' is a normal verb, so questions take 'do': Do we need.
